t: Dynamic Tag Generator: a plain-language overview
title: Dynamic Tag Generator: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Dynamic Tag Generator does and why archives need it. A dynamic tag generator reads a record and invents the labels that describe it — topics, names, places, dates. It picks the words that matter most and turns them into searchable tags. Every record gets richer the moment it arrives, with no human tagging required.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Dynamic Tag Generator works
title: How the Dynamic Tag Generator works
description: Overview: what the Dynamic Tag Generator does and why archives need it. Real taggers extract keywords with TF-IDF or TextRank, pull named entities (people, places, organizations) as entity tags, and add metadata-derived tags (year, file type, collection). Each tag carries a confidence score, and only tags above a threshold are applied; the rest wait in a suggestion queue. Tag vocabularies are controlled — new tags map to canonical forms via the synonym registry — so 'NYC' and 'New York City' do not become two different tags.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Dynamic Tag Generator works: the deep tour
title: How the Dynamic Tag Generator works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Dynamic Tag Generator does and why archives need it. Real taggers extract keywords with TF-IDF or TextRank, pull named entities (people, places, organizations) as entity tags, and add metadata-derived tags (year, file type, collection). Each tag carries a confidence score, and only tags above a threshold are applied; the rest wait in a suggestion queue. Tag vocabularies are controlled — new tags map to canonical forms via the synonym registry — so 'NYC' and 'New York City' do not become two different tags. Advanced taggers learn per-collection tag priors, suppress near-duplicate tags ('car' vs 'cars') by stemming, and measure quality by tag precision against human-tagged samples plus search-success lift. The limits are subjective tags ('beautiful', 'important') which the engine refuses to invent, and sparse records with too little text — those get metadata-only tags with their thin evidence noted rather than speculative content tags.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
